name: Mona Lisa
hook: The world's most famous portrait, and the 1911 theft that turned it into a household name.

facts.label: Leonardo da Vinci
facts.statement: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, beginning around 1503. He was born in the Tuscan town of Vinci and later studied lip muscles in a Florence morgue.

facts.label: Lisa Gherardini
facts.statement: The sitter is generally identified as Lisa Gherardini, wife of the Florentine merchant Francesco del Giocondo — hence the title La Gioconda.

facts.label: the Louvre
facts.statement: The painting hangs in the Louvre in Paris. In the 17th century it was in Louis XIV's suite before becoming the museum's star attraction.

facts.label: the 1911 theft
facts.statement: Vincenzo Peruggia stole it from the Louvre in 1911, hiding it for two years before he was caught trying to sell it in Florence.

facts.label: the smile
facts.statement: Her enigmatic smile is the painting's trademark. She may have lost her eyebrows to a careless cleaning, and Leonardo studied lip muscles to get the expression right.

facts.label: Marcel Duchamp
facts.statement: Marcel Duchamp's readymade L.H.O.O.Q. is a reproduction of the Mona Lisa defaced with a penciled mustache and goatee.
